lead.zh-Hans: 一种颜色的名字，把我写到了下一行。
lead.en: One colour’s name carried me onto the next line.

text.zh-Hans: 看旧金山金门大桥时，我把 International Orange 写在便纸上，没预留好，Orange 只好去下一行。旅人问两行是不是两种颜色。我赶紧把它们圈在一起。这么长的名字，我想念完整一次寄给你，别让一种颜色在路上分家。
text.en: Looking at the Golden Gate Bridge, I ran out of room for “International Orange.” A traveler wondered whether the two lines named two colours. I circled them together. I want to say the whole name for home, so one colour does not split into two on its journey.
Say the colour’s full name
Frame the two written lines

lead.zh-Hans: 轮子在转，今天不用我的脚帮忙。
lead.en: The wheels turned without any assistance from my feet.

text.zh-Hans: 在旧金山缆车博物馆的参观区域，我看动力设备带着地下缆索运转。自己站着没动，眼睛倒很忙。我想在纸上画个转动记号，画到一半，差点把它当成给你的笑脸。先收好，离馆后再分清哪个是轮子，哪个是我。
text.en: From the visitor area at the Cable Car Museum, I watched machinery move the underground cables. My feet stayed still; my eyes were busy. A rotation mark on paper nearly became a smiling face. After leaving, I can decide which part is the wheel and which part is me.
Talk about the wheels afterward
Follow the curve of the arrow

lead.zh-Hans: 面包有嚼劲，我的一句话也跟着慢。
lead.en: Chewy bread slowed down a sentence too.

text.zh-Hans: 吃旧金山酸面包时，我正想对旅人讲一句很长的话。外皮需要认真嚼，我便把话停好，吃完再继续。等轮到开口，忘了中间几个词，反而讲得简短。菜单上记了酸味和嚼劲，信里就省掉那段绕远的句子。
text.en: A bite of San Francisco sourdough interrupted a sentence I was preparing for a traveler. The crust deserved some chewing. By the time I could speak, a few words had escaped and the sentence was better for it. The menu records tang and chew. You have been spared the much longer sentence.
Say the shorter sentence
Read the texture notes

lead.zh-Hans: 汤可以装碗，香味暂时不肯装信封。
lead.en: The bowl held the soup. The envelope declined the aroma.

text.zh-Hans: 旧金山的番茄海鲜炖汤，让我想写一封带香味的信。试着形容了半页，还是只有字。我先把 cioppino 和自己这碗见到的鱼虾记在菜单上，换张干净纸给你写信。香味留给记忆，这回不用信封加班。
text.en: Cioppino in San Francisco made me want to send a scented letter. Half a page of description still produced only words. I noted the dish and the fish and shrimp in my own serving on the menu, then found clean paper for home. The aroma can stay in memory; the envelope has enough work.
Choose a phrase for the soup

text.zh-Hans: 看看画里自己的这一碗
text.en: Look at this particular bowl

lead.zh-Hans: 旅人问午饭，我先把嘴里的吃完。
lead.en: Asked about lunch, I finished the bite first.

text.zh-Hans: 有人问我在旧金山吃了什么，我把酸面包和海鲜炖汤的菜单递过去，先把嘴里的那口吃完。对方看图等我。我终于不用一边嚼一边点头，能完整说出两样名字。给你的家信也算练过了，读到菜名时不用猜我的含糊声。
text.en: Asked what I had eaten in San Francisco, I handed over the sourdough and cioppino menus while finishing a bite. My listener studied them and waited. Then I could give both names properly, without nodding and chewing. This letter home has benefited from the rehearsal.
Say both names clearly
Notice how the menus illustrate them

lead.zh-Hans: 一张画得宽，一张画得深。
lead.en: One drawing went wide, the other deep.

text.zh-Hans: 酸面包占了旧金山菜单的横向，汤碗占了另一张的纵向。收进小纸套时，两个方向闹了点别扭。我把菜单各转半圈，才发现自己也跟着歪头。我摆正脑袋，重新折纸套，原来不必让午饭替我迁就每条折痕。
text.en: The sourdough spread across one San Francisco menu; a deep soup bowl filled the other. Packing them together made me tilt both paper and head. I straightened up and refolded the sleeve instead. Lunch need not accommodate every fold I happen to make.
Tell how tilting your head helped
Inspect the refolded sleeve

lead.zh-Hans: 我照“{reply}”练了一遍，才写上卡片。
lead.en: I practiced “{reply}” before making the card.

text.zh-Hans: 按你的回应，我把 International Orange 从头到尾念完，再写在自己做的长纸签上。旁边只有我画的金门大桥轮廓，没有冒充标准色样。读完整个名字时，纸签刚好够长。旧金山这一笔颜色，终于不用分行跟你打招呼。
text.en: Following your reply, I said “International Orange” in full and wrote it on a long homemade label. Beside it is my Golden Gate Bridge outline, not a paint-standard swatch. The paper finally fits the name. This bit of San Francisco can greet home without breaking into two lines.
Read the label for home
Check the lines this time

lead.zh-Hans: 手套没丢，我却捡回了别人的那只。
lead.en: My mittens were both on. I still picked up someone else’s.

text.zh-Hans: 那只橙红手套刚落地，我就伸手去捡，嘴里还嘀咕自己怎么丢了东西。主人看看我的双手，笑着问我是不是多长了一只。我这才发现自己的手套全戴着。重来旧金山，金门大桥熟悉的橙红色让我认路，却没帮我认准手套。我赶紧道歉，对方伸手来接，三只橙红手套挤在了一起。
text.en: An orange-red mitten fell nearby, and I picked it up, wondering aloud how I had managed to lose it. Its owner looked at my hands and asked whether I had grown an extra one. Both my own mittens were still on. I had recognised the Golden Gate Bridge’s familiar orange-red colour on this return to San Francisco, but that had hardly helped me identify my belongings. I apologised and handed it over. For a moment, three orange-red mittens were crowded together.

text.zh-Hans: 说说多出来的手套是谁的
text.en: Explain who owns the extra mitten

text.zh-Hans: 数数我们手里的橙红手套
text.en: Count the orange-red mittens between us
